newsitem.title: USA: J. Baker sees after-tax $117 mln charge.
newsitem.headline: J. Baker sees after-tax $117 mln charge.

text.p: J. Baker Inc said Tuesday that it will take an after-tax charge of about $117 million for the restructuring of its footwear operations.

The non-recurring charge is associated with the disposal of the Parade of Shoes and Shoe Corporation of America divisions, as well as the write-down of assets related to the restructuring of its Licensed Discount footwear operations.

The charge, said the company, will be taken in the fourth quarter of the fiscal year ended February 1. Managament said that it expects the charge will have a positive impact on the future liquidity of the company.

The company said it has completed the previously-announced sale of its Parade of Shoes division to Payless ShoeSource Inc for about $20 million, as well as the the sale of its Shoe Corp of America division for about $40 million. The proceeds will be used to pay down bank debt, the company said.
J. Baker, Inc is a diversified retailer of apparel and footwear operating 439 Casual Male Big & Tall stores, 66 Work 'n Gear stores, 875 licensed footwear departments in discount department stores.
